gbm_population_evidence.quote: Primary supratentorial glioblastoma with first or second rogression/recurrence

candidate_evidence.quote: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of camrelizumab \[a programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) inhibitor\] combined with bevacizumab for adult patients with recurrent glioblastoma.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Primary supratentorial glioblastoma with first or second rogression/recurrence

role_evidence.quote: Phase 2: Targeted combined immunotherapy: once every three weeks with the following drugs: (1) bevacizumab 7.5mg/kg intravenously;(2) Carrelizumab: 200mg/ time, intravenous infusion.
Stage 1: Targeted therapy induction phase: bevacizumab 5mg/kg, intravenous infusion, once every two weeks, 2 cycles in total.
In this study, the combination therapy was optimized by introducing induction phase therapy, which is expected to further improve the efficacy.

coder_notes: Single registered intervention 'Camrelizumab and Bevacizumab' split into two moieties. Camrelizumab is the only non-established agent, so experimental_monotherapy on a bevacizumab backbone. Bevacizumab coded established_therapy_experiment because its new induction schedule is named as part of the optimisation; soc_backbone is the alternative (no effect on candidate status). Both arms are experimental (first vs second relapse), no control.
